- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to lag or overshoot upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.2) — model often fails to capture sharp downward moves or mean reversion.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — model frequently overcorrects after sharp price increases, leading to overshoots.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to underestimate sustained upward trends and overestimate downward corrections.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to underestimating late-period momentum, especially when sentiment is rising.
- Lag correction: model often lags 1–2 days behind true price action, especially in high volatility or sentiment-driven moves.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.6, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast; if sentiment < 0.3, subtract 0.5–1.0% to account for underreaction.
